title: "Endpoint Deployment Pipelines"

## {{< fa rocket >}} Endpoint Deployment Pipelines

After machine learning models are trained and registered in Azure Machine Learning, separate GitHub Actions workflows are used to deploy them as real-time online endpoints.

In this project, two endpoint deployment workflows are implemented:

| Endpoint                   | Purpose                                                                |
| -------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Linear Regression Endpoint | Performs real-time taxi fare prediction.                               |
| KMeans Clustering Endpoint | Groups similar taxi trips into clusters based on trip characteristics. |

Both deployment workflows follow the same deployment architecture but use different endpoint and deployment configuration files depending on the model being deployed.

---

## {{< fa sitemap >}} Endpoint Deployment Architecture

The endpoint deployment workflows are executed manually using GitHub Actions.

```yaml id="cvw3s8"
on:
  workflow_dispatch:
```

This allows users to deploy or redeploy endpoints on demand directly from the GitHub Actions interface.

### Common Deployment Workflow

Both endpoint deployment pipelines perform the following tasks:

1. Read Azure configuration values.
2. Authenticate GitHub Actions with Azure.
3. Install the Azure Machine Learning CLI extension.
4. Register the Azure ML environment if required.
5. Create the online endpoint.
6. Remove any existing deployment.
7. Create a new deployment.
8. Route traffic to the deployment.
9. Test the endpoint using sample data.
10. Display endpoint information.

```{mermaid} id="pk1k4z"
flowchart TD

A[GitHub Actions Trigger] --> B[Authenticate with Azure]
B --> C[Install Azure ML CLI]

C --> D[Create Endpoint]
D --> E[Delete Existing Deployment]

E --> F[Create New Deployment]
F --> G[Route Traffic]

G --> H[Test Endpoint]
H --> I[Display Endpoint Details]
```

---

# {{< fa chart-line >}} Linear Regression Endpoint

The first deployment workflow publishes the trained Linear Regression model as an Azure Machine Learning Online Endpoint.

```yaml id="fwv9zf"
name: Deploy Model Endpoint

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
```

### Purpose

This endpoint provides real-time taxi fare predictions.

Applications can submit trip-related features and receive a predicted fare amount from the deployed model.

---

## Create Endpoint

The workflow creates the Azure ML endpoint using:

```bash id="g1y8n7"
az ml online-endpoint create \
  --file ML/endpoint.yaml
```

### Purpose

The endpoint acts as the public entry point through which applications can send prediction requests.

The endpoint configuration is defined in:

```text
ML/endpoint.yaml
```

This file contains:

* Endpoint name
* Authentication configuration
* Endpoint settings
* Deployment routing configuration

---

## Create Deployment

After the endpoint is created, a deployment is created.

```bash id="6r5k2m"
az ml online-deployment create \
  --file ML/deployment.yaml \
  --all-traffic
```

### Purpose

The deployment contains:

* Registered model
* Scoring script
* Azure ML environment
* Compute configuration

The deployment configuration is stored in:

```text
ML/deployment.yaml
```

The option:

```text
--all-traffic
```

routes 100% of incoming requests to the newly deployed version.

---

## Endpoint Testing

The workflow validates the deployment by sending a sample prediction request.

```bash id="y5h1e2"
az ml online-endpoint invoke \
  --name taxi-mlops-endpoint \
  --request-file ML/sample-request.json
```

### Purpose

This confirms that:

* The endpoint is running.
* The scoring script executes successfully.
* Predictions are returned correctly.

Successful execution indicates that the fare prediction endpoint is ready for use.

---

# {{< fa-project-diagram >}} KMeans Clustering Endpoint

The second deployment workflow publishes the trained KMeans clustering model as a separate Azure Machine Learning Online Endpoint.

```yaml id="9xj2r7"
name: Deploy KMeans Cluster Endpoint

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
```

### Purpose

This endpoint classifies taxi trips into clusters based on trip characteristics.

Examples include:

* Airport trips
* Short-distance trips
* Long-distance trips
* Peak-hour journeys

---

## Create Endpoint

The clustering endpoint is created using:

```bash id="p8m4d6"
az ml online-endpoint create \
  --file ML/endpoint-kmeans.yaml
```

### Purpose

This file contains the endpoint configuration specific to the clustering model.

```text
ML/endpoint-kmeans.yaml
```

---

## Create Deployment

The deployment is created using:

```bash id="m4s8q3"
az ml online-deployment create \
  --file ML/deployment-kmeans.yaml \
  --all-traffic
```

### Purpose

The deployment configuration specifies:

* Registered KMeans model
* Scoring logic
* Environment configuration
* Compute resources

All traffic is directed to the deployment after creation.

---

## Endpoint Testing

The clustering endpoint is validated using sample taxi trip data.

### Sample Request

```json id="c7h5k9"
{
  "DOLocationID": 161,
  "fare_amount": 12.50,
  "trip_distance": 2.1,
  "passenger_count": 1,
  "pickup_hour": 9
}
```

The request is sent using:

```bash id="r2v7n1"
az ml online-endpoint invoke \
  --name taxi-cluster-endpoint \
  --request-file /tmp/kmeans-request.json
```

### Purpose

The deployed model analyzes the input data and returns the predicted cluster assignment.

This allows applications to identify groups of similar taxi trips in real time.

---

# {{< fa cogs >}} Common Deployment Logic

Although the deployed models differ, both workflows follow the same deployment pattern.

---

## Step 1: Create Endpoint

```bash id="t4m6z8"
az ml online-endpoint create \
  --file <endpoint-yaml-file>
```

### Purpose

Creates the Azure Machine Learning Online Endpoint.

The endpoint acts as the publicly accessible API entry point for prediction requests.

If the endpoint already exists, the workflow continues without failing.

---

## Step 2: Delete Existing Deployment

```bash id="n8p3q6"
az ml online-deployment delete \
  --name blue \
  --endpoint-name <endpoint-name> \
  --yes
```

### Purpose

Removes the existing deployment named **blue**.

Benefits include:

* Preventing deployment conflicts.
* Ensuring a clean deployment state.
* Simplifying redeployment workflows.

---

## Step 3: Create Deployment

```bash id="h7k9s2"
az ml online-deployment create \
  --file <deployment-yaml-file> \
  --all-traffic
```

### Purpose

Creates a fresh deployment containing:

* Registered model
* Environment
* Scoring script
* Compute configuration

The deployment becomes the active endpoint version.

---

## Step 4: Test Endpoint

```bash id="j5r2m4"
az ml online-endpoint invoke \
  --name <endpoint-name> \
  --request-file <sample-request-file>
```

### Purpose

Validates the deployment by sending sample data to the endpoint.

This confirms that:

* The endpoint is reachable.
* The model loads successfully.
* Predictions are generated correctly.

---

## Step 5: Display Endpoint Details

```bash id="q1n6z5"
az ml online-endpoint show \
  --name <endpoint-name> \
  --query "{name: name, scoring_uri: scoring_uri, state: provisioning_state}" \
  -o table
```

### Purpose

Displays deployment information including:

* Endpoint Name
* Scoring URI
* Provisioning State

The Scoring URI is later used by external applications such as the Streamlit frontend to obtain real-time predictions from the deployed model.

---

# {{< fa exchange-alt >}} Deployment Workflow Summary

The complete deployment process follows the sequence below:

```{mermaid} id="5mpf1x"
flowchart LR

A[Registered Model] --> B[GitHub Actions Workflow]

B --> C[Create Endpoint]
C --> D[Delete Existing Deployment]
D --> E[Create New Deployment]

E --> F[Route Traffic]
F --> G[Test Endpoint]

G --> H[Display Endpoint Details]
H --> I[Ready for Real-Time Predictions]
```

---

# {{< fa clipboard-check >}} Summary

The Endpoint Deployment Pipelines take trained and registered models from Azure Machine Learning and make them available for real-time inference.

Two independent deployment workflows are implemented:

| Workflow                   | Purpose                                  |
| -------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| Linear Regression Endpoint | Provides real-time taxi fare prediction. |
| KMeans Clustering Endpoint | Provides real-time taxi trip clustering. |

Both workflows use GitHub Actions and Azure Machine Learning deployment configurations to automate endpoint creation, deployment, validation, and traffic routing.

This approach ensures that model deployments are:

* Automated
* Repeatable
* Consistent
* Easy to redeploy
* Suitable for production-style MLOps workflows

Once deployed, the endpoints can be consumed by external applications such as dashboards, APIs, and Streamlit frontends for real-time machine learning predictions.
